title: Equidimensional closed fibre of a finite type domain over a valuation ring
statement: Let $A$ be a valuation ring, meaning an integral domain such that for each nonzero $a\in K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ either $a\in A$ or $a^{-1}\in A$, and put $k=A/\mathfrak m_A$ for its residue field. Let $D$ be an integral domain containing $A$ as a subring and finite type as an $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Form the algebras $D_k=D\otimes_Ak$ and $D_K=D\otimes_AK$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with multiplication $(d\otimes a)(e\otimes b)=de\otimes ab$. If $D_k\ne0$, then $\dim D_k=\dim D_K$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], and $\operatorname{Spec}D_k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is equidimensional: every irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] has topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] equal to $\dim D_K$.

source.place: Tag 00QK (lemma-finite-type-domain-over-valuation-ring-dim-fibres), statement including its final equidimensionality assertion

proof.text: Put $F=D\otimes_AK$ and $E=D\otimes_Ak$. By [lem-trf-domain-generic-local-fibre-bound], $F$ is a nonzero finite type domain and $d=\dim F=\operatorname{trdeg}_K\operatorname{Frac}(F)$ is a finite integer; $E$ is finite type over $k$. Fix any prime $Q$ of $E$. The ring $A$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_A$: if $a,b\in A$ are non-units and both nonzero (otherwise $a+b$ is one of them), after swapping $a/b\in A$, so $a+b=b(1+a/b)$ is a non-unit; hence the non-units form an ideal. Localizing at $\mathfrak m_A$ therefore inverts only units, so $\kappa(\mathfrak m_A)=k$. The same node with this prime gives the finite integer $n=\dim_Q\operatorname{Spec}E$ and $d\le n$.

Apply [lem-trf-localized-polynomial-chart-fibres] to $A,D,Q,n$. It supplies $g$, $B=D_g$, $\alpha:A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\to B$, and its two field-fibre maps $\alpha_K$ and $\alpha_k$, finite type and quasi-finite. Here $B$ contains $A$ and is a domain, $H=B\otimes_AK$ has fraction field identified over $K$ with $\operatorname{Frac}(F)$, and $T=B\otimes_Ak$ is finite type over $k$ with a point $Q_g$ of local dimension $n$.

source.place: Tag 00QK (lemma-finite-type-domain-over-valuation-ring-dim-fibres), quasi-finite chart and its two fibres

proof.text: If $d<n$, then $\operatorname{trdeg}_K\operatorname{Frac}(H)=d<n$ by steps 1–2. Apply [lem-trf-valuation-generic-relation-specialization] to $\alpha$, with $A\subset B$ the domain inclusion from step 2. It gives $h\in\ker\alpha$ with a coefficient $1$, whose reduction $\bar h$ is nonzero and satisfies $\alpha_k(\bar h)=0$. Apply [lem-trf-quasi-finite-polynomial-kernel-dimension-drop] to $\alpha_k:k[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\to T$: its target and map are finite type and the map is quasi-finite at every prime by step 2. Thus $\dim\operatorname{Spec}T<n$. But $n=\dim_{Q_g}\operatorname{Spec}T\le\dim\operatorname{Spec}T$: the whole spectrum is one open neighbourhood in the defining minimum [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]. This contradiction gives $n\le d$, hence $n=d$.

source.place: Tag 00QK (lemma-finite-type-domain-over-valuation-ring-dim-fibres), residue relation and strict dimension-drop contradiction

proof.text: The prime $Q$ was arbitrary, so every point of $\operatorname{Spec}E$ has local dimension $d$. The dimension-as-supremum-of-local-dimensions theorem [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions] gives global dimension $d$; this is a nonempty supremum because $E\ne0$: [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] states that absence of prime ideals is equivalent to being the zero ring. [lem-weil-pbc-spec-topological-krull-dimension-ring] then gives $\dim E=d=\dim F$. For equidimensionality, [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes] writes each component as $V(\mathfrak p)$ for a minimal prime $\mathfrak p$ of $E$. At the point $\mathfrak p$, this is the unique component containing it: a component $V(\mathfrak r)$ through it has $\mathfrak r\subseteq\mathfrak p$, hence $\mathfrak r=\mathfrak p$ by minimality. Since $E$ is finite type over the field $k$ by step 1, [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-components] identifies the dimension of that component with $\dim_{\mathfrak p}\operatorname{Spec}E=d$. This proves every clause.
